knowledge-base.name: fw-echo
knowledge-base.triggers: Echo, echo framework, labstack/echo, github.com/labstack/echo, echo.Context, echo.HandlerFunc, echo.MiddlewareFunc, echoMw, echo.New, Go REST API, go echo, .go echo
knowledge-base.overview: Echo v4+ guardrails, patterns, and best practices for Go REST APIs. Covers application setup, route grouping with versioning, built-in and custom middleware, context usage, request binding with go-playground/validator, custom validators, consistent JSON response envelopes, domain error mapping, and graceful shutdown. Loaded automatically when agents work on Echo-based .go files.

core-principles.principle: handler -> service -> repository. Handlers are thin HTTP adapters; business logic is in services only.
Register a custom validator on e.Validator at application startup. Always Bind then Validate as separate steps.
Prefer Echo's built-in middleware (Recover, Logger, RequestID, CORS, Gzip, RateLimiter, Secure) before writing custom alternatives.
Return the same JSON envelope on every endpoint. Never expose internal errors to clients.
Always implement e.Shutdown(ctx) with signal handling.

guardrail.rule: Always Bind then Validate as two separate steps. Never skip Validate after Bind.
guardrail.bad: if err := c.Bind(&req); err != nil { return err } // No c.Validate call — validation skipped

guardrail.rule: Register custom validator on e.Validator at startup. Raw go-playground/validator errors must not reach clients.
Never store business logic in handlers. Never import echo in service or repository layers.
Never expose internal errors to clients. Map domain errors to HTTP status codes in handlers only.
Register Recover() first in middleware chain to catch panics in all subsequent handlers.
Use c.Request().Context() when passing context to services or repositories.
guardrail.bad: userService.GetByID(c, id) // passing echo context to service

guardrail.rule: Type-assert values from c.Get() with an ok check. Never assume the type without checking.
Use pointer fields for optional partial-update request structs.
Configurable middleware functions return echo.MiddlewareFunc (a function that takes and returns echo.HandlerFunc).

knowledge-base.project-structure:
myproject/ ├── cmd/ │ └── api/ │ └── main.go # Entry point ├── internal/ │ ├── config/ │ │ └── config.go │ ├── handler/ │ │ ├── handler.go # Handler container │ │ ├── user.go │ │ └── auth.go │ ├── middleware/ │ │ ├── auth.go # JWT middleware │ │ └── custom.go # Custom middleware │ ├── model/ │ │ ├── user.go │ │ └── response.go │ ├── repository/ │ │ ├── repository.go │ │ └── user.go │ ├── service/ │ │ ├── service.go │ │ └── user.go │ └── validator/ │ └── validator.go # Custom go-playground/validator wrapper ├── pkg/ │ └── response/ │ └── response.go ├── migrations/ ├── .env.example ├── go.mod └── Makefile
Layer responsibilities: - handler/ HTTP: parse, validate, call service, write response - service/ Business logic — no echo or HTTP imports - repository/ Data access; accepts context.Context - model/ Domain structs, request/response DTOs - middleware/ Custom echo middleware functions - validator/ Custom validation rules

pattern.name: Application Setup
pattern.example:
e := echo.New() e.HideBanner = true e.Validator = validator.NewCustomValidator()
e.Use(echoMw.Recover()) e.Use(echoMw.Logger()) e.Use(echoMw.RequestID()) e.Use(echoMw.CORSWithConfig(echoMw.CORSConfig{ AllowOrigins: cfg.CORSOrigins, AllowMethods: []string{http.MethodGet, http.MethodPost, http.MethodPut, http.MethodPatch, http.MethodDelete}, AllowHeaders: []string{echo.HeaderOrigin, echo.HeaderContentType, echo.HeaderAccept, echo.HeaderAuthorization}, }))

quick-reference.item: c.Bind then c.Validate — always both steps
c.Request().Context() to services; c.Get/c.Set for request-scoped values
Return errors from handlers; centralized via echo.HTTPErrorHandler
Consistent Response envelope; c.NoContent for deletes
BodyLimit() for oversized requests; built-in RateLimiter()
